questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to model partitioning with a derived block metric that is additive via a simple prefix, and to present a workable DP with reconstruction.

## Key Concepts
- Partition DP
- Prefix sums
- Backtracking reconstruction
- Complexity: O(n^2 k)

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode for transitions
for i in 1..n:
  for t in 1..k:
    dp[i][t] = max_{j<i} dp[j][t-1] + (P[i]-P[j])
    back[i][t] = argmax_j
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you reconstruct the exact blocks from the DP table?
- Any edge cases when n < k or all increases are zero?

## Why This Is Asked
Design a DP that handles partitioning with a per-element penalty, enabling exact k blocks with reconstruction; this variant extends standard partition DP by a linear per-element cost and a prefix-sum transform.

## Key Concepts
- DP over fixed-k partitions
- Prefix sums with a constant penalty transform
- Running bestPrev to achieve O(nk) time
- Traceback pointers for block endpoints

## Code Example
```javascript
const n = A.length;
const S = new Array(n+1).fill(0);
for (let i=1; i<=n; i++) S[i] = S[i-1] + A[i-1];
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How to extend to at most k blocks or include negative penalties?
- Can you optimize space to O(n) per k without losing reconstruction?

Why This Is Asked
This checks ability to derive a non-trivial tree DP with knapsack merging over children, handling exact k paths and reconstruction.

Key Concepts
- Tree DP on rooted graphs
- Knapsack merge across multiple children
- Disjoint-path constraints and reconstruction
- Complexity considerations

Code Example
```javascript
function dfs(v, p) { dp[v] = Array(K+1).fill(-INF); dp[v][0] = 0; for (const u of adj[v]) if (u !== p) { dfs(u, v); /* merge dp[v] and dp[u] */ } }
```

Follow-up Questions
- How to extend to weighted endpoints penalties?
- How to reconstruct endpoints efficiently?
- What are time/memory bounds for N up to 2e5 and K up to N?
